The proposed repair prevents accidental resets, but **immediately rejecting every v1 request without a mask breaks the six-month support commitment**. Requiring masks can be a valid future contract; it needs a compatible transition.

The supplied [contract](project/contract.json) explains the [recorded incident](project/incident.json): an omitted `updateMask` selects **all mutable fields**. The captured rename supplies only `displayName`, so the absent selected scalars take their defaults:

- `displayName` becomes `"Summer"`.
- `description` becomes `""`.
- `spendLimitMicros` becomes `"0"`.

That after-state is a supplied observation, not a result reproduced during this review. The request conforms to the provider’s omission semantics but fails the caller’s rename intent. HTTP PATCH alone does not imply preservation of omitted fields; this custom contract controls the behavior.

quotes.quote:
The repair should preserve a supported v1 path through an adapter or coexisting interface while newer requests use explicit masks. An adapter needs established operation intent: map rename to `displayName` and description reset to `description`. Merely selecting every field v1 knows is unsafe—selecting `displayName,description` for the captured rename would still clear the description.

A rule based only on populated fields also needs a defined reset representation. An omitted description cannot, by itself, distinguish “leave unchanged” from “clear.” The supplied files do not establish whether deployed v1 clients can emit masks, explicit empty strings, or a separate reset operation. Those capabilities remain unverified; the repair must resolve them without forcing an immediate upgrade of supported clients.

Also settle **empty-mask behavior**, which the supplied contract does not explicitly define. Exercise supported client/provider combinations during rollout and rollback, including the adapter if chosen. Assign migration ownership and use verified client inventory plus observed affected-operation usage to support retirement after the six-month window; quiet telemetry alone cannot account for offline or infrequent clients.
